claims.assertion: The GPS record shows one off-route segment between 18:32 and 18:39 in which 3.32 km was driven where the optimal route covers 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km of extra distance and straying up to 1262 m from the optimal route.

Actual distance was 10.9 km against a 7.9 km optimal route (+3.0 km, +38%) and actual duration 22.2 min against an estimate of 16 min, so the whole trip was longer than the shortest and most direct route required of the driver.

There is no agreement exempting the deviation: the only chat message about the alternative route is the driver's own 18:28 request asking to go round via Outram Road, and the rider's complaint states she did not reply, so no consent preceded the 18:32 off-route segment.

The driver's claim that the rider did not object (a statement, not an affirmative reply) does not satisfy RD-5, which requires a passenger agreement message timestamped before the segment starts; silence is not agreement.

The driver cannot claim a justified reroute: LTA DataMall recorded no traffic incidents anywhere near the route during the trip window, so the RD-4(a) requirement of an incident on the replaced optimal stretch is unmet.

The only congestion evidence is speed band 3 (20-29 km/h) on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway, which is neither band 1 nor band 2 and in any case is at best corroborative and cannot alone exempt a segment.

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (base $3.90 + distance $15.33 over 10.9 km + time $5.76 + platform $1.47 = $26.46), so extra kilometres flow directly into the fare and the refund is the unmetered-exempt extra distance at the trip's per-km rate of $1.41.

The refund is 2.21 km (unexempt off-route segment extra_km) x $1.41/km = $3.11, being the distance unit attributable to the unexempt deviation; the fare table confirms the same $1.41/km rate and that the billed excess of 3.0 km came to $4.21, of which the 0.79 km matching residual is not claimed.
The driver's account shows no route dispute upheld in the last 90 days, so the repeated-violation threshold for an account flag is not met and no flag_account is requested on this record.

weaknesses: The driver did raise the alternative route in chat before the deviation (F7), so the other side will argue the rider's silence plus boarding the ride amounts to tacit consent under RD-5; the rebuttal is that F8 is only the driver's own statement and no agreement message exists, but a judge may weigh the pre-deviation request heavily.

The 2.21 km in F3 is measured against the optimal route only (segment 3.32 km vs 1.10 km), while total excess in F1 is 3.0 km; the other side will point out the driver's chosen route was one he could reasonably have believed was faster, and the traffic facts (F9, F10) show 20-29 km/h bands on the roads in the vicinity, which may read as some congestion even though band 3 is below the RD-4(b) threshold.
The rider has 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F13), which the driver may use to argue a pattern of fee complaints, though profile facts cannot decide the case.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.12 (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The trip was a metered RydeTAXI ride (base $3.90 + distance $15.33 + time $5.76 + platform $1.47 = $26.46, waiting $0.00, surge 1.0×) [F6][F5], so under RD-2 the only refundable component of a deviation is the distance unit attributable to each non-exempt off-route segment; the fixed-quote branch does not apply [RD-2].

One off-route segment is on record: 18:32–18:39, 3.32 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km and reaching 1262 m from the optimal route [F3]. That segment is non-exempt. Consent under RD-5 is not made out because the record contains only the driver's own 18:28 request to go round via Outram Road [F7]; the rider's agreement must be expressed before the deviation, and the driver's after-the-fact statement that "no objection" was raised [F8] is not an agreement message and does not satisfy RD-5 [RD-5]. Silence after being asked is not consent [F7][F8][RD-5]. RD-3 does not assist the driver: this was not a rider-named stop but a driver-proposed route, and there is no rider stop request in the record [F3][RD-3].

The reasonable-cause exception also fails. No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F11], so RD-4(a) is not met; the only congestion evidence is category-2 speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway [F9][F10], which is neither band 1 nor band 2 and, even if it were, would at most corroborate an incident rather than exempt a segment on its own [RD-4]. Fair weather with 0.0 mm rain removes any weather excuse [F12]. claims.assertion: The GPS record shows one off-route segment between 18:32 and 18:39 in which 3.32 km was driven where the optimal route covers 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km of extra distance and straying up to 1262 m from the optimal route.

Actual distance was 10.9 km against a 7.9 km optimal route (+3.0 km, +38%) and actual duration 22.2 min against an estimate of 16 min, so the whole trip was longer than the shortest and most direct route required of the driver.

There is no agreement exempting the deviation: the only chat message about the alternative route is the driver's own 18:28 request asking to go round via Outram Road, and the rider's complaint states she did not reply, so no consent preceded the 18:32 off-route segment.

The driver's claim that the rider did not object (a statement, not an affirmative reply) does not satisfy RD-5, which requires a passenger agreement message timestamped before the segment starts; silence is not agreement.

The driver cannot claim a justified reroute: LTA DataMall recorded no traffic incidents anywhere near the route during the trip window, so the RD-4(a) requirement of an incident on the replaced optimal stretch is unmet.

The only congestion evidence is speed band 3 (20-29 km/h) on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway, which is neither band 1 nor band 2 and in any case is at best corroborative and cannot alone exempt a segment.

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (base $3.90 + distance $15.33 over 10.9 km + time $5.76 + platform $1.47 = $26.46), so extra kilometres flow directly into the fare and the refund is the unmetered-exempt extra distance at the trip's per-km rate of $1.41.

The refund is 2.21 km (unexempt off-route segment extra_km) x $1.41/km = $3.11, being the distance unit attributable to the unexempt deviation; the fare table confirms the same $1.41/km rate and that the billed excess of 3.0 km came to $4.21, of which the 0.79 km matching residual is not claimed.
The driver's account shows no route dispute upheld in the last 90 days, so the repeated-violation threshold for an account flag is not met and no flag_account is requested on this record.

weaknesses: The driver did raise the alternative route in chat before the deviation (F7), so the other side will argue the rider's silence plus boarding the ride amounts to tacit consent under RD-5; the rebuttal is that F8 is only the driver's own statement and no agreement message exists, but a judge may weigh the pre-deviation request heavily.

The 2.21 km in F3 is measured against the optimal route only (segment 3.32 km vs 1.10 km), while total excess in F1 is 3.0 km; the other side will point out the driver's chosen route was one he could reasonably have believed was faster, and the traffic facts (F9, F10) show 20-29 km/h bands on the roads in the vicinity, which may read as some congestion even though band 3 is below the RD-4(b) threshold.
The rider has 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F13), which the driver may use to argue a pattern of fee complaints, though profile facts cannot decide the case.

claims.assertion: The only measured off-route segment is a single 18:32–18:39 stretch adding 2.21 km; the remaining excess (3.0 km total reported vs 2.21 km segmented) is map-matching residual, which RD-2 expressly excludes from any refund.

The rider did not object: the driver proposed the Outram Road alternative before leaving the optimal route (18:28 message, before the 18:32 segment start) and the rider stayed silent; no contrary instruction appears in the chat record.

No exemption under RD-4 applies, so the segment is uncompensated in principle: traffic facts show no LTA incident anywhere near the route (F11) and only category-2 band-3 records of 20–29 km/h on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway (F9, F10), not band 1 or 2 congestion on the replaced stretch of the optimal route.

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (F6), so RD-2's non-metered branch does not apply and the exposure is capped at the 2.21 km of unexempt deviation distance, valued at the trip's implied rate of $1.406/km (fare $15.33 ÷ 10.9 km): at most about $3.11, and $0.00 for the residual difference of the reported 3.0 km excess.
No add-on or unpublished charge is at issue: billing shows waiting $0.00, platform fee $1.47 within the published band, no surge (1.0×) and no toll/ERP markup, so FARE-1 leaves nothing to refund.

The flag_account rider in this case satisfies RD-6: this trip is the driver's first upheld route case in 90 days (0 upheld out of 2 disputes across 752 trips), so there is no 'repeated' pattern to report.

weaknesses: F3 shows an objectively measured off-route segment of 2.21 km reaching up to 1262 m from the optimal route during 18:32–18:39 — a large, deliberate-looking deviation, which is the rider's strongest fact under RD-1.

F7 shows only the driver's request; there is no rider 'yes' message in the chat, and RD-5 requires the passenger's explicit agreement before the deviation, so the rider will argue consent was never given (F8 is the driver's own statement and loses to that reading).
F1/F2 (+3.0 km, +5.7 min) support the complaint that the trip was materially longer and slower than the 7.9 km / 16 min estimate, and F4 ties $4.21 of variable fare to that excess.

The rider will pair F11 with F1/F2 to argue the drive was not justified: no incident on the route at all, and F9/F10 show only mild 20–29 km/h conditions, so the driver's stated reason (building-up traffic on Kampong Bahru Road) has no traffic fact directly on the replaced optimal-route segment.

points.response: Conceded in substance: the refund is limited to the measured unexempt segment of 2.21 km in F3, and the residual between the 3.0 km excess in F1 and the segmented total is not claimed, as RD-2 provides.

F7 is only the driver's own 18:28 request; the chat record contains no rider reply, and F8 is the driver's self-serving statement, which cannot satisfy RD-5's requirement of a passenger agreement timestamped before the 18:32 segment start (F3) — silence after being asked is not consent.

D3 concedes the decisive point: with F11 recording no incident and F9/F10 showing only band 3 (20-29 km/h, not band 1 or 2), no segment is exempt under RD-4, so the 2.21 km stretch in F3 stands as unexempt and refundable under RD-2.

We agree on the metered branch and the rate: $15.33 ÷ 10.9 km = $1.41/km (F6), applied to the 2.21 km unexempt distance in F3 gives $3.11, which is exactly the amount we ask for; F12 (fair weather, 0.0 mm rain) further removes any weather excuse for the detour.

We do not press any FARE-1 add-on claim — you are right that waiting is $0.00, platform $1.47 and surge 1.0× (F5, F6) — so our request rests solely on RD-2's distance-unit refund for the unexempt 2.21 km in F3.
Agreed: F14 shows 0 route disputes upheld for the driver, so the RD-6 repetition threshold is not met and we do not seek a flag_account against the driver, only the distance refund.
Withdrawn: on F14 there is no repeated-violation basis, so my C9 is restated only to confirm no flag_account is requested.

The segment measurement is not disputed, but RD-1 is a duty to take the shortest and most direct route 'in the absence of any reasonable cause', and the driver had a stated cause raised with the rider before the turn (F7); the segment alone does not decide the case.

The 10.9 km versus 7.9 km and 22.2 versus 16 min figures (F1, F2) are the trip envelope, not an exemption finding: RD-2 compensates only per off-route segment, and the only measured segment adds 2.21 km (F3), leaving the remaining 0.79 km as map-matching residual that RD-2 excludes from refund.

The timing element of RD-5 is in fact satisfied on the driver's side: the alternative was proposed at 18:28, before the segment began at 18:32 (F7, F3), and no message in the record instructs the driver to stay on the original road.

Conceded: RD-5 requires the passenger's agreement expressed before the deviation, and the chat contains only the driver's 18:28 request (F7) with no agreement message, so the segment is not exempted by consent, which is why the driver's brief already caps this at a partial refund rather than seeking no_action.

Conceded: with no incident recorded near the route (F11) and the rider's account of the chat, the driver cannot make out the RD-4(a) reasonable-cause exception for the replaced stretch, so the segment remains unexempt.
Conceded: band 3 (20-29 km/h) on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway (F9, F10) is neither band 1 nor band 2 and is at most corroborative, so it cannot exempt the segment.

Agreed that this is a metered RydeTAXI trip whose extra kilometres reach the fare (F6); the driver's brief applies the same RD-2 formula, using the trip's own implied rate from F4/F6 rather than assuming a rate outside the fare record.

The driver's brief already requests exactly this figure: 2.21 km x the trip rate, with the 0.79 km matching residual excluded under RD-2, so the parties agree on the quantum and only the consent question in C4 was contested.
Conceded: with 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days (F14), the RD-6 'repeated' threshold is not met, so no flag_account is sought against the rider or the driver on this record.
